title: libidinal economy
summary: A reading of social life in which desire is treated as a scarce, investable force — circulated, hoarded, and spent the way capital is.
whyItMatters: It names why attention, status, and sexual energy show up in markets and politics as if they were prices, not leftovers. Useful when a ‘rational’ model keeps missing what people are actually allocating.
notes: The phrase is locked to Lyotard’s Économie libidinale (1974), though the move is older: Freud already talked about psychic ‘economics.’ A sharp lens; easy to over-apply as a just-so story about every institution.
